Container.Name: isputnik
Container.Overview:
Private self-hosted family media library, now in Beta (4.0.0 and later). Audiobooks with a built-in player, ebooks with an in-browser reader, and a photo and video gallery with face recognition (the isputnik-faces container beside it, nothing leaves your server), albums, slideshows rendered to MP4, and a Photo Inbox for scans and photos from relatives. The family writes its own stories and recipes around what the house holds, and keeps a family tree linked to the people found in the photos. Multiple accounts with per-person progress and permissions, sharing and guest links, passkeys and two-factor sign-in, an installable PWA with offline listening, and an English or Russian interface.
Beta means your data is looked after: the database migrates itself forward on every upgrade, a copy of it is saved before each new version starts, and backups can be scheduled from the Control panel. Features are still moving. On first run, open the web UI on your home network to create the administrator account.
Container.Changes:
### 2026.11.10 — 4.78.1 System data is chosen for you - **A new install no longer stops at the Storage page before its first library.** Home now takes the folder next to its database as system data when it first starts: `/config` in Docker, the `data` folder beside the app otherwise. Before, every new install had to open Control panel → Library → Storage and confirm that same suggested folder before any library could be created, and the page did not say so until you tried. - You can still change it on the Storage page; thumbnails, backups and metadata follow it as before. An install that already has system data or libraries is not touched, and a suggested folder the app cannot write to is still left for you to choose.
### 2026.11.09 — 4.78.0 Quality for viewers away from home - **A Quality menu in the video player.** Beside Sound and Subtitles: **Original**, **1080p**, **720p** or **480p**. Pick a smaller one on a weak Wi-Fi corner or a phone and the engine makes that picture while you watch, from where the film is; a film already smaller than the rung plays as it is. The choice is remembered in that browser, one for home and one for away, and the next film starts in it. - **Viewers away from home are held under a cap.** Someone watching from outside your network starts at **Quality away from home** (Settings → Video → Converting video; up to 720p to start with) and can only go lower. Before, a Blu-ray rip went out at its full 30 Mbit/s or more, which no home upload link carries, and stalled; one viewer at 720p needs about 5 Mbit/s. Set it to *The file as it is* to turn the cap off. At home everyone still gets the file as it is unless they pick less. - **The engine now looks at a film's size, not only its codecs.** A picture taller than the rung asked, or heavier than the most the rung would make, is re-encoded down to it even when a browser could have played it as it is. The *Converting video* card marks each viewer's rung beside GPU/CPU and HDR. Needs **isputnik.video 0.31.0**; an older engine shows no menu and no setting. - The TV app is unchanged: on the home network it plays the original as before. Automatic switching by connection speed and per-film offline copies are planned, not built (`docs/video-quality-plan.md`).
### 2026.11.09 — 4.77.0 Photos on the TV - **Photos come to the TV, as a controlled view.** A TV may be watched by more people than the photos' owners, so it never gets the whole gallery: only the slideshows and albums an admin puts on its list. No folders, timeline, people or search. - **On TV, on the Photos page.** Admins find it on the Albums and Slideshows views: add a slideshow or an album, put them in the order the TV shows them, and take one off again (nothing is deleted). Each line says which profiles see it: **Everyone but restricted profiles** (the default), **Everyone**, or **Only…** chosen profiles and "Without a profile". That is how *Kids* gets Grandma's birthday album and nothing else. - **A person's own access still applies on top.** The list only ever narrows: a photo the person signed in can't open on the website never shows on the TV, even inside a picked album. A slideshow's rendered movie plays on the TV only when the viewer may see every photo in it; otherwise the TV plays the slideshow live, with just their photos. - **A TV can't wander off the list.** A TV's session reads only its list's albums and slideshows, their photos and videos, their music and allowed movies; everything else in Photos is refused, and it can change nothing. - The TV app's **Photos** tab arrives in **iSputnik TV 0.11**: a banner and rows of slideshows and albums, a full-screen viewer with each slideshow's own timing and transitions, music, videos playing in place, and a caption with the date, place and who is in the photo. The tab appears only when something is on the list for the profile watching.
### 2026.11.09 — 4.76.0 Who's watching - **Viewing profiles, as on Netflix.** An admin sets up the household's ways of watching video — *Kids*, *Russian*, *Classic* — on the video page under **Customize › Profiles**. Each has a name, a colour, the video libraries it shows and rows of its own (set on its tab in Customize; until then it shows the household's rows). - **Every TV and browser can watch as a profile.** The TV app asks **Who's watching?** when it opens, and the video page has a **Watching as** menu. A profile only ever narrows what the person signed in may see — search, title pages and sets show nothing outside its libraries — and it changes Video only: photos, books and the rest of the app stay the account's. - **Each profile keeps its own history.** Continue watching, watched marks and My list belong to the profile, the same on every TV whoever is signed in, so the cartoons stay out of the grown-ups' Continue watching. Without a profile, everything is your own, as before. - **Restricted profiles and a household PIN.** Getting into *Kids* is free; getting out needs the PIN, set by an admin with their password (4 to 8 digits; 5 wrong tries lock entry for 15 minutes). On a TV the PIN also guards choosing another person linked on it, linking someone new and unlinking. Without a PIN, the Profiles tab says that anyone can still switch away. - Profiles made in the short-lived **Profile › TV profiles** tab that slipped into 4.73.1 become household profiles, and a TV wearing one keeps it. - The video engine needs its own update for profiles to keep their own history: **isputnik.video 0.30**. An older engine keeps working, and a profile then shares the history of whoever is watching. The TV app's profiles and PIN pad come in **iSputnik TV 0.9**.
### 2026.11.08 — 4.75.0 Who was at the door - **A failed sign-in now names the person and the device.** Security › Sign-ins used to gather every failed attempt under *Not signed in*, because a wrong password proves nothing about who typed it — but it does say whose account was tried. Each failed attempt now counts against the account whose name was typed, in the People table and in that person's own dive, and the attempts table shows the browser or phone it came from, with the account's name under the address. Names that match no account still gather under *Not signed in*. Attempts logged before this update are matched up by the name they tried; the device they came from was never recorded. - **A locked account shows on the page.** Being refused at a locked account counted nowhere, so an account could be locked for half an hour while Sign-ins looked quiet. Those refusals now count as failures with a **Locked out** result, the Failed card says how many there were, and the person's row says **Locked out now** with an unlock button — the same rescue as Members › Users. - **4.74.0 never reached the image registry.** Its build failed on a lint check over the Library mockup scripts in the docs folder, which are prototypes rather than the app; they are now excluded from the check, and ten database-upgrade tests that the Stremio removal had left failing are fixed. This release carries everything 4.74.0 announced, including the removal of the Stremio add-on.

Config.Name: Web UI Port
Config.Description: Port used to access the iSputnik web interface.

Config.Name: Config & Data
Config.Description: Stores database, metadata, thumbnails, backups, settings, and application data. Backups appear here under backups/.

Config.Name: Media Storage
Config.Description: Media storage path. Must be Read/Write — uploading photos/videos and filing them into dated folders writes here (scanning alone only needs read). Additional storage locations can be added later by editing the container or from within iSputnik.

Config.Name: PUID
Config.Description: User ID the app runs as. The server runs unprivileged (not root); on first start it takes ownership of the Config & Data path as this user. 99 (nobody) matches the default owner of an Unraid appdata share — leave it unless your share is owned by a different user.

Config.Name: PGID
Config.Description: Group ID the app runs as. 100 (users) matches the default group of an Unraid appdata share — leave it unless your share uses a different group.

Config.Name: App URL
Config.Description: The address the app is reached at (for example https://isputnik.example.com). Set this when you put a reverse proxy or tunnel in front: it fixes the browser origin the app accepts, and an https address is also what turns on HTTPS-only enforcement (HSTS). Leave blank for plain LAN access.

Config.Name: HSTS
Config.Description: Leave blank. When App URL starts with https:// the app tells browsers to stay on HTTPS for a year. Set to false to suppress that — for example when your reverse proxy already sends its own Strict-Transport-Security header. Nothing is sent for a plain-http App URL either way.

Config.Name: Cookie Secure
Config.Description: Leave on auto: secure cookies then follow App URL — on when it starts with https://, off for a plain http home install. Set true or false only to override that. Secure cookies are never sent over plain http, so forcing true on an http install drops the sign-in cookie and you cannot log in. (auto needs version 1.13.3 or newer.)

Config.Name: Session Length (days)
Config.Description: Number of days a login session remains valid.

Config.Name: Linked Device Session Length (days)
Config.Description: Number of days a TV, wall display or other screen signed in with Link a device stays signed in. Each one is listed under Profile, Devices and can be revoked there.

Config.Name: Invite Validity (days)
Config.Description: Number of days invitation links remain valid.

Config.Name: Trusted Proxy Addresses
Config.Description: The reverse proxy's own IP or CIDR range, comma-separated for several (e.g. 172.18.0.0/16 for a Docker network). Preferred over Trusted Proxy Hops: forwarded headers are only believed when they come from these addresses. Leave blank for direct LAN access. Needed for correct per-IP rate limiting, auto-block, and trusted networks.

Config.Name: Trusted Proxy Hops
Config.Description: Alternative to Trusted Proxy Addresses when the proxy's IP isn't fixed: the number of reverse proxies in front of the app (usually 1 behind a reverse proxy or Cloudflare Tunnel). Leave blank for direct LAN access or when Trusted Proxy Addresses is set (addresses win if both are). Set it to match your proxy count, no higher, and don't expose the app's port directly.
